pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered his own reasoning back into the pillar rather than just accepting it: "Because like you said, that was an eliminated excuse in itself. And so it's like, no, I just, let's just go get this. And I know I have the time. The time isn't something I'm worried about. It's more that I have the time, but then because I don't have the workout in mind or written down, I don't really know what to do. So I'll just not do anything or I'll go and doom scroll on my phone." He also volunteered that the minimalism appeals — "he's not asking me to go join the fanciest gym."

Tied it directly to his own failed experiment and articulated why this framing fixes it: "I tried the carnivore diet for a while... it was extremely restrictive for going out. My wife did not like dating me... So being able to live a little is good" and "I need to find something sustainable." No pushback on losing the after-work snacks, which was the habit he had already identified as his worst.

The pillar he came for and the one he reacted hardest to: "I'm excited that it has an app, because that'll be easier to find... it's always good to be able to see visual progress, but also, like you said, that accountability is just a click away as well... it's better to fill my phone with stuff that's going to help me." He had opened the entire call with "It's more for the accountability side of it" and had explained he does not want that burden falling on his wife.

anchors.raw: I don't charge people the basement price because I don't want them to expect basement outcomes. I want them to expect what I plan to deliver, which is something good that they're going to appreciate and that's going to last. And so I understand that part.
anchors.note: The prospect argued the seller's case for him from his own construction business, and separately endorsed price-as-commitment: "it's enough to where it's definitely gonna hurt if you waste it." This is the strongest supportive anchor anywhere in the batch and the rep did not build on it — it arrived at 00:52:49 and the conversation moved to scheduling.

anchors.raw: it's the most I've ever spent on something fitness-wise. So even if you count, like, years of gym membership.
anchors.note: His entire lifetime fitness spend is the comparison class, and $6,000 exceeds all of it. He also has a membership he still pays for and which provides childcare while he trains, so the offer has to beat something he is already getting value from.

anchors.raw: there's other things that I think she'd probably rather spend money towards, like that amount of money. So there's certain amounts where it's like we just don't talk about, because it's small enough where it's like, okay, I trust you
anchors.note: He has a personal discretionary threshold below which no conversation is required, and $6,000 sits well above it. That threshold — never asked for — is the number that would have told the rep whether an instalment structure could have closed this on the call.

anchors.raw: I've just been watching a lot of Trevor's videos and I've even got some kettlebells myself and I've just been starting to do stuff with them
anchors.note: Fourth prospect in the batch entering through free content with equipment already bought and progress already made. He states the self-directed path explicitly as his fallback: "I'm going to figure out a way whether or not I can do this or not... It's probably just going to take me longer."

unmet_demand.want: A payment structure that splits the $6,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never offered. His only stated blocker was the size of a single payment relative to a household threshold, and instalments and deposits are demonstrably available — the same rep referenced a six-instalment plan and a deposit internally the previous day.

unmet_demand.want: Equipment guidance — whether to buy more kettlebells, and whether to get adjustable ones
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked explicitly and directly in his opening answer: "I've got two kettlebells in there at a set weight. Like, do I need to get a couple more? Should I invest in one of those multi, like, weighted ones that you can select? I'm like, I don't know." It was never answered at any point in 61 minutes, including in the presentation. The programme almost certainly covers this — nobody said so.

unmet_demand.want: A way to bring his father-in-law, wife and four-year-old daughter into it with him
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised the father-in-law twice unprompted and it is a genuine driver ("just so he can do that as long as he wants to, not just until his body says he can't"), plus his wife's lapsed Olympic lifting and play kettlebells for his daughter. The offer is a single-person one-to-one transformation with no family, partner or referral structure described.

unmet_demand.want: A route into helping others professionally, given his health and exercise science degree and interest in being a client success story
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised twice — "if this is something too that could be another avenue for me to share or to help other people, like I have a background in it" and "if I were to be able to get to do that, that'd be cool too." The rep acknowledged the pass-it-on framing generically but nothing concrete exists.
